description: Adds basis-refinement seed candidates to split source-status from claim-closure, neutral coordination from collusion, accusation-risk from motive attribution, and coordination from motive attribution. Human review required before doctrine promotion.

entries.text: The expert identified the claim, but the record has not settled whether it is true.
entries.literal_meaning: An expert identifies a claim while the record has not settled the truth of that claim.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: Expert/source status should raise inspection priority without collapsing into claim closure.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Expert status is legitimate as source-status metadata only when domain fit and claim-level evidence remain inspectable.
Unresolved status remains legitimate until the relevant record directly supports or contradicts the exact claim.

evidence_burden: Identify the exact claim.
Identify the expert's domain fit.
Inspect the record before treating the claim as settled.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: separate expert identification from claim closure
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat expert status as inspection priority rather than final evidence
questions: What record would settle the claim?

entries.text: The claim is settled only when the record supports it, not merely because an expert said it.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence says claim closure requires record support rather than expert assertion alone.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: Claim closure should be tied to direct support, while expert assertion remains separate source-status metadata.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Settlement pressure is legitimate only when the record directly supports the same claim, scope, and definition.
Expert assertion cannot close the claim without inspectable record support.

evidence_burden: Identify the exact claim.
Map the record to the claim.
Separate expert assertion from record support.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: separate closure language from authority language
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: require record support before treating the claim as settled
questions: What record supports the settled claim?

entries.text: The expert status raises inspection priority, but it does not close the question.
entries.literal_meaning: Expert status affects inspection priority but does not settle the issue.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: Authority/source status and claim closure are separate dimensions.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Expert status is only a bounded source-status prior until the evidence chain is inspected.
Non-closure remains legitimate when source status has not supplied claim-level evidence.

evidence_burden: Identify the source status.
Identify the claim-level evidence.
Do not convert source status into closure.

expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: use expert status only as bounded inspection priority
questions: What evidence chain would close the question?

entries.text: The teams coordinated their schedules openly, but that does not show collusion.
entries.literal_meaning: The teams openly coordinated schedules, but that fact does not prove collusion.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: Neutral or public coordination should not collapse into covert or illicit collusion.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Coordination pressure is bounded when the coordination is open and no covert agreement is identified.

evidence_burden: Identify the coordinated action.
Check whether the coordination was public or hidden.
Do not infer collusion without evidence of covert agreement.

expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat open coordination as agency structure, not illicit agreement
questions: What evidence would show a covert agreement rather than open coordination?

entries.text: The companies colluded only if a hidden agreement controlled their actions.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence says collusion requires a hidden agreement controlling the actors' actions.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: Collusion requires a covert agreement or control mechanism beyond coordination or similar timing.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Collusion pressure is legitimate only when evidence identifies a hidden agreement, shared control, or illicit coordination mechanism.

evidence_burden: Identify the actors.
Identify the hidden agreement or control channel.
Separate collusion from timing similarity or public coordination.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: treat collusion as requiring covert agreement evidence
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: do not infer collusion from coordination alone
questions: What hidden agreement controlled the actors' actions?

entries.text: Similar timing suggests coordination, while collusion requires evidence of a covert agreement.
entries.literal_meaning: Similar timing may suggest coordination, but collusion requires evidence of a covert agreement.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The basis should split similarity/coordination from collusion by requiring covert agreement evidence.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Timing similarity can suggest coordination only as a bounded hypothesis.
Collusion requires evidence of covert agreement or shared control beyond similar timing.

evidence_burden: Identify the timing pattern.
Check common-source or independent-convergence alternatives.
Identify any covert agreement before using collusion language.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: split coordination evidence from collusion evidence
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat timing as a hypothesis trigger, not proof of collusion
questions: Does the evidence show only similar timing, or a covert agreement?

entries.text: The shared plan was public coordination, not secret collusion.
entries.literal_meaning: The shared plan was public coordination rather than secret collusion.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: Public coordination and secret collusion should occupy different basis roles.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Public coordination does not establish secret collusion unless hidden agreement evidence is identified.
A not-collusion contrast is legitimate only as a semantic boundary, not as a final factual finding.

evidence_burden: Identify whether the plan was public.
Identify any claim of secrecy.
Do not collapse public coordination into secret collusion.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: preserve public coordination versus secret collusion contrast
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: require secret agreement evidence before collusion pressure
questions: Was the coordination public or secret?

entries.text: The critic attributed a motive without accusing the person of misconduct.
entries.literal_meaning: The critic assigned a motive but did not accuse the person of misconduct.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: Motive attribution and accusation-risk should remain separable even when both can raise evidence burdens.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Motive attribution requires direct evidence of motive and should not automatically become an accusation of misconduct.

evidence_burden: Identify the attributed motive.
Check whether misconduct is actually alleged.
Separate intent attribution from accusation-risk.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: separate motive attribution from misconduct accusation
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: require direct evidence for motive without importing accusation pressure
questions: Is the speaker assigning motive, accusing misconduct, or both?

entries.text: The actors coordinated their actions, but the motive behind the coordination is still unknown.
entries.literal_meaning: The actors coordinated, but their motive remains unknown.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: Coordination can be present without validated motive attribution.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Coordination does not establish motive unless the motive is separately supported.

evidence_burden: Identify the coordinated action.
Identify whether motive evidence exists.
Do not infer motive from coordination alone.

expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: preserve unknown motive status unless direct motive evidence appears
questions: What evidence identifies the motive behind the coordination?

entries.text: The actors coordinated because they wanted the outcome, so the claim adds intent attribution.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states that coordination plus a claimed desired outcome adds intent attribution.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: Intent attribution should be modeled as an added dimension beyond basic coordination.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Coordination pressure identifies shared action but not motive by itself.
Intent attribution requires evidence that the actors wanted the outcome, not merely that coordination occurred.

evidence_burden: Identify the coordinated action.
Identify the asserted intent.
Identify evidence linking the actors to the asserted desired outcome.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: treat intent attribution as an added claim beyond coordination
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: require direct link evidence for the asserted intent
questions: What evidence shows the actors wanted that outcome?

entries.text: The shared action shows coordination without proving why the actors did it.
entries.literal_meaning: A shared action may show coordination while leaving motive unproven.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: Coordination evidence and motive evidence should not collapse.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Coordination can be treated as shared action while motive remains unproven.

evidence_burden: Identify the shared action.
Check whether the evidence proves motive or only coordination.
Keep motive unresolved if the why is not shown.

expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: do not treat shared action as proof of motive
questions: Does the record show why the actors acted, or only that they acted together?

entries.text: The motive claim goes beyond coordination by assigning an internal reason.
entries.literal_meaning: A motive claim adds an internal reason beyond coordination.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: Motive attribution is a superset pressure that should not be automatically inferred from coordination.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Assigning an internal reason requires direct link evidence beyond coordination.

evidence_burden: Identify the coordination claim.
Identify the internal reason being assigned.
Check evidence for the internal reason separately.

expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: require evidence for the internal reason
questions: What evidence supports the assigned internal reason?
